overall: The AG found the Weston School Committee properly convened in open session before executive session on June 3 and 17, but violated the OML by failing to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals and by approving February 4 minutes late; a generalized allegation was declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee convened in executive session before open session at its June 3 and June 17 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Absent evidence to the contrary, we credit the public body’s statement and find that the Committee convened its meetings and conducted the required procedural steps in open session before entering executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee had not periodically reviewed its executive session minutes to determine whether continued nondisclosure was still warranted.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to review its outstanding executive session minutes at reasonable intervals.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the minutes of the February 4 meeting were not approved in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Committee did not approve meeting minutes for its February 4 meeting until August 28 despite meeting more than three times in the intervening months.

allegations.summary: Generalized complaint that minutes are sometimes not posted promptly or completely and agendas are sometimes titled incorrectly, with no specific date or wrongdoing.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent that this allegation does not allege any particular wrongdoing by the Committee on a specific date, we decline to review this allegation because our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
